name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Indianapolis-based district leans about 21 points Democratic
Incumbent Carson has a large money edge; the Republican shows no reported fundraising
Kalshi and Polymarket both price Carson's reelection at 97-98%
No public polling; a Libertarian on the ballot may trim the margin slightly
model.rationale: A district leaning 21 points Democratic, a well-funded incumbent facing a challenger with no visible fundraising, and markets pricing the Democrat at 97-98% all point the same way, so this stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican fundraising or a sharply favorable national environment for Republicans could narrow the margin, though an upset would still require an unusual shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's Seventh District is anchored in Indianapolis and leans about 21 points Democratic, making it one of the most Democratic seats in the state. André Carson, the incumbent, is seeking another term and has raised about $1.1 million with roughly $600,000 on hand. His Republican opponent, Patrick McAuley, shows no reported fundraising, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and markets. Kalshi and Polymarket both price Carson's reelection around 97 to 98 percent. The expected margin is roughly 24 points for Carson, with wide uncertainty given the absence of polling. Nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race; the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
